title: Process what will not store, team up, and prove your results

say: Process what will not store, team up, and prove your results.
This is the video for Module 3 of Post-Harvest Management and Food Preservation.
Some produce will not store fresh. Yams cut by the hoe, cassava that must be used within days, fish landed in the heat. Instead of watching it rot, you can turn it into a product that lasts.

panel.heading: Five ways to make food last longer
items: Drying: yam chips, cassava chips, okra
Smoking: catfish, mackerel
Salting: salted dried fish
Fermenting: garri, fufu, iru
Cooling: leafy vegetables, fish on ice

say: Drying removes the water that moulds need. Smoking dries and coats the food. Salting draws water out and stops many germs.

say: Fermenting uses friendly microbes, as in garri and iru. And cooling slows breathing and germ growth.

say: Open sun drying on the ground lets in dust, insects, goats and rain. A solar dryer is a box or tent with a clear cover and air vents. The cover keeps all of that out.

panel.heading: Drying chips safely
items: Wash hands and tools, slice on a clean board
Cut pieces to an even thickness
One thin layer on raised mesh trays
Dry until pieces are hard and snap
Cool, pack airtight, label with date
Check stored chips regularly

say: Wash your hands and tools, and slice on a clean board, not the floor. Cut pieces evenly so they dry at the same rate, and spread them thinly on raised trays.

panel.heading: Drying chips safely

say: Dry until each piece snaps cleanly. Cool, then pack at once in clean, airtight containers, labelled with the product and date.

say: Any soft piece needs more time. And any batch that shows mould must be thrown away.

panel.rule: Soft or bendy pieces need more time. Mould means discard.

say: When fat drips onto flames, or fish sits in thick dirty smoke, harmful compounds called PAHs build up on the fish. Improved kilns keep the fire separate and catch the fat.

panel.heading: Keep the fire away from the fish
left: Keep flames away from the fish
right: Let fat drip onto open flames
Burn plastic, tyres or painted wood

say: Whatever kiln you use, never burn plastic, rubber, tyres or painted wood.

say: Cut yams will not store, so Funmi must decide this week. Selling them all now brings 60,000 naira.
First she runs a small trial. 10 kg of yam gives her 2.5 kg of dry chips, a yield of 25 percent in her own hands.

card.title: Funmi: sell cut yams or dry them?

say: So 150 kg should give about 37.5 kg of chips. At about 2,500 naira per kg, that is 93,750 naira. Her costs for firewood, labour, transport and bags are about 15,000.

card.title: Funmi: sell cut yams or dry them?

say: Processing leaves 78,750 naira, which is 18,750 more than selling fresh. It pays only because she measured her own yield and costs first. With no time or no buyer, selling the same day is still better.

card.title: Funmi: sell cut yams or dry them?

say: Some tools cost too much for one household. Extension officers from your state ADP, and NSPRI, the stored products research institute, can advise and train.

panel.heading: Share the cost and the knowledge

cards.d: Your state ADP officers advise on drying, storage and pests, and run field demonstrations.
Shared equipment, bulk buying, group storage and selling, with written rules.
Say who you are, what you measured, what you need and when. General requests get little.

say: In a group, costs shrink. One group of 15 women shared a moisture meter quoted at about 120,000 naira. That is 8,000 naira each, with written rules on who keeps it and how it is booked.

say: Your evidence pack shows the loss point, your baseline, the change, the result measured the same way, the value minus the cost, and a 90-day plan.

panel.heading: Extend, add, share, review
items: Weeks 1 to 4: use the method on all the crop
Weeks 5 to 8: add a second improvement
Weeks 9 to 12: help three other women measure
Week 13: review records, update your pack

say: For example, Ifeoma sells garden egg near Nsukka. Her plan uses the new routine on every trip, adds a clay pot cooler, shows four other sellers her method, and updates her pack in week 13.

say: Her loss fell from 12 percent to 5 percent. That is a fall of 7 percentage points, not 7 percent. Saying it correctly avoids confusion.

panel.rule: Report the change in percentage points.

say: Check your pack. Same storage time as the baseline, or the result looks bigger than it is. Subtract the cost. Say prices are approximate. Use several trips, not one good day. Add photos and dates.
If something did not work, say so. Honest records build trust.

panel.heading: Avoid these report mistakes
items: Same storage time as the baseline
Cost of the change subtracted
Prices marked approximate
Average of several trips
Photos and dates included

say: To remember. Process food that spoils fast and has buyers, but trial it first. Keep fish away from flames. Ask partners for something specific. And measure before and after with the same method.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Process food that spoils fast and has buyers
Trial first: measure yield and costs
Keep fish away from flames and fat
Ask partners for something specific
Same method before and after
